idiom_name: core object + abstract role base + specification-keyed role trader/registry
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep the key abstraction (Component) as an interface with the shared operations plus a minimal role protocol (add/get/remove/has by specification), and implement it in a ComponentCore that owns a specification-keyed map of roles. Every role derives from an abstract ComponentRole that holds a reference to the core and re-exposes the Component operations by forwarding to it (the Decorator part, applied without chaining roles). Role instances are created only by the core, through a trader mapping specifications to creators, so the core never mentions a concrete role class; clients request a role and cast to the concrete role interface. Give the core deliberate ownership of its roles and provide identity comparison so core and role views of the same subject compare equal.
code_sketch:
core = CustomerCore(customer_id)              # Component implementation; owns its roles
core.addRole("Borrower")                     # spec -> role trader -> new Borrower(core)
if core.hasRole("Borrower"):
    borrower = cast(core.getRole("Borrower"), Borrower)
    borrower.securities()                    # role-specific view of the same logical object
# ComponentRole implements the Component interface by forwarding to core:
#   Borrower.getAccounts() -> core.getAccounts()
pitfalls: Creating roles outside the core (clients calling role constructors) lets role objects exist without a core and breaks identity and lifetime.
Forwarding only operations means attribute changes must be propagated to affected roles explicitly; silent state divergence is the pattern's classic failure.
Letting the role protocol grow into a general-purpose property bag; keep it to add/get/remove/test by specification.

Wrong move: testing 'same object' with ==, equals() or identity hashes on roles -> two clients holding different role views of one subject get logical duplicates in sets, caches and query results -> instead put an explicit core/identity comparison (sameCoreAs, or compare cores) on the Component interface and key collections on the core.

Wrong move: implementing role creation as an if/switch over specification values inside the core -> every new role forces an edit and redeploy of the core, silently killing the open/closed decoupling the pattern exists to buy -> instead keep specification-keyed creators in the role trader so a new role touches only the registry.

Wrong move: letting any client detach or delete a role while other clients still hold that role view -> survivors keep references to a detached or destroyed role and observe stale or dangling behaviour -> instead make detachment a deliberate core-owned operation (core destroys roles with itself; consider refcounts or an explicit release protocol) and forbid clients from deleting roles they did not create.
